summary: A changelog page and a what's-new widget: Markdown entries rendered to a static page and RSS, a badge that knows the last entry a visitor saw, and a script that posts new entries to Slack. One of the smallest real products on the list and a good first build.

prerequisites.name: Node.js 22 or newer
prerequisites.why: Everything in this build runs on it: the server, the scripts, the tests.
prerequisites.get: Download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, or install with your package manager (brew install node, or nvm install 22). Restart the terminal afterwards.

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: A static host, or your existing site
prerequisites.get: Cloudflare Pages, Netlify, or a folder in your current site.

env.name: SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL
env.where: For the publish script. Empty disables it.

phases.title: The page
phases.goal: Entries rendered newest first with categories; a validating build; RSS.

steps.do: changelog/YYYY-MM-DD-slug.md with frontmatter (title, date, category) and build.mjs
commands: mkdir changelog && cd changelog && git init && npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module && npm install markdown-it@14 gray-matter@4

steps.do: Render index.html and feed.xml; fail on a missing field naming the file

check: Adding an entry and rebuilding shows it first
A missing field fails the build

phases.title: The widget
phases.goal: A badge from latest.json cleared by opening the panel.

steps.do: The build writes latest.json with newest date and count; widget.js shows a badge on data-changelog
A panel listing the last five entries; localStorage for the seen date in try/catch

check: A new entry makes the badge appear
The page works with the widget blocked

phases.title: Design
phases.goal: A timeline, category colours, dark mode, no style leaks.

steps.do: Timeline layout and category colours with dark mode
Scope the widget's styles so nothing leaks into the host page

check: The panel does not alter host page styles

phases.title: Distribution

steps.do: A publish script posting a new entry to SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL
Guard against re-posting an entry already announced

check: A new entry appears in Slack within a minute

phases.title: Deploy
phases.goal: One command from Markdown to live; README.

steps.do: README: frontmatter reference and the one-line embed

check: An entry goes from Markdown to live with one command

phases.title: Private changelog
phases.goal: A customer-only changelog behind your app's login.

steps.do: Serve the built HTML from your app behind its existing auth
Per-plan entries via a frontmatter field the build filters on

check: A logged-out visitor cannot see the private changelog
A plan-tagged entry shows only to that plan

product.outcome: Product updates your users actually see, with a widget you own and an optional private track.
releaseGate: Widget verified on a host page without style leaks

notIncluded: The hosted editor and reaction analytics.
after: Reactions stored in a tiny endpoint
